promptAsSent:
Use the image_gen tool to generate exactly one image, then stop. Do not write files, run commands or edit anything.

Attached reference images, in order:
Image 1: Geometry/layout authority
Image 2: Identity: the intact stones, their material, colour, light and rendering

Use case: sketch-to-render. RESKIN image 1, the authoritative geometry guide, into the DESTROYED state of seven overhead field-stone groups for a top-down tactical game: each stone blasted apart into a low scatter of broken chunks lying where it stood. Image 2 is the intact sheet and is the IDENTITY authority: the same painterly stone, the same soft upper-left light. Image 1 says where every chunk lies.
Preserve image 1 exactly: 2:1 canvas, 4 columns x 2 rows, the eighth frame (bottom right) EMPTY. Paint one broken rock chunk on every grey shape in the guide, at its place and size, and small gravel on the guide's dots; leave the guide's open ground open. Do not join the chunks back into a stone and do not add chunks.
Camera STRAIGHT DOWN from directly above, orthographic plan view, as in image 2.
Chunks are angular fresh breaks with fractured faces and weathered outer faces, lit from the upper left, lying low and flat. Keep image 2's corroded olive-grey stone with its yellow-green stains and sulphur-crusted pits; fresh breaks show the same dark stone, a shade lighter at most, never pale. Stay as dark as image 2. Muted: the scatter should read as rubble on the ground, quieter than the intact stones. It must read clearly at about 50 pixels across: distinct chunks, no fine noise.
No grass, soil, crater, scorch disc, ground patch or cast shadow outside the chunks, no labels, no text, no border. True transparent background around and between every chunk. Keep the 2:1 canvas.

references.role: Identity: the intact stones, their material, colour, light and rendering

agentMessages: I’ll use the imagegen skill to render one transparent rubble sheet, preserving the guide’s chunk layout and the intact stones’ material.
